title: 2015 AMC 8 Problem 7
statement: Each of two boxes contains three chips numbered \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3.\) A chip is drawn randomly from each box and the numbers on the two chips are multiplied. What is the probability that their product is even?

solutions.text:
The product is odd only when both chips are odd. Each box has two odd chips, \(1\) and \(3,\) out of three chips, so the probability of an odd product is \((\dfrac23)^2=\dfrac49.\)

The probability of an even product is the complement, \(1-\dfrac49=\dfrac59.\)

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: It may be easier to count the complement: an odd product.
The product is odd only if both drawn chips are odd.
